SELECTED TARGET

Home / start

01 / 20
No hardware movement

Crawl moves one foot at a time (slow, very stable); tripod moves three at once (L1, L3, R2 then R1, R3, L2), about twice as fast with three feet always down. Insect gaits walk continuously like a real insect: legs swing forward on an arc while the others push, staggered back to front; use a short Transition (150–250 ms) and no easing for smooth walking. Set Hip swing above 0 to size steps as a hip rotation in degrees instead of stride. Stand/Sit use the posture settings below and hold motor torque. Building a template replaces the current sequence; save edits first.

06 Tune on the robot

ROBOT ENABLED · SUPPORT THE BODY

Jog a foot · touch-down & teach

Lower the foot until it just touches the ground, then save its height as that leg’s Stand trim. To teach a pose, jog the feet into place and add it to the sequence. Hip −/+ turns the foot around its hip, keeping its reach and height. Keys: ↑/↓ raise/lower, ←/→ X, [ / ] hip, when no field has focus. Each jog moves over 0.5 s.

—

Step one servo slowly toward its end stop and stop when it strains or buzzes; back off a few degrees and use that as the limit. Testing a servo leaves the legs off the planned pose, so use Enable at home before moving again. Limits apply to all six legs and are saved on the board.

Release one leg

Turns off only that leg’s three servos to free it; the other legs keep holding. Use Enable at home before moving again.

PHYSICAL ROBOT

Plan first. Move when ready.

No live command data. Angles and positions are model targets, not feedback sensors.

Play / Send / Stand / Sit use the speed and easing; Repeat applies to Play. Transitions stay within 100–10,000 ms; under 300 ms the servos may not keep up. The preview uses the same settings.

LIVE WALK · IK ON THE BOARD

Walk continuously

The board computes every foot’s path and runs inverse kinematics every 20 ms, so the robot walks smoothly instead of stepping between poses. Press a direction to start, another to steer (curves too), ■ to slow down and stop in the starting stance. Step height, speed and stride angle can be changed while walking; the robot blends into them over about one step. Keys: W A S D, Q / E turn, X stop.

Set up Motion Studio on your Servo 2040 +
  1. Keep your previous calibration folder as a backup. In Thonny, save these four files to the board root: . This replaces the board’s main.py with training mode. Keep your existing calibration_offsets.json on the board.
  2. Support the body with all feet clear. Run check_and_restart.py in Thonny. Close Thonny, then reconnect USB without holding BOOTSEL.
  3. Use desktop Microsoft Edge or Chrome. Click Connect robot, choose its USB/COM port, and verify your preview with the loaded board calibration.
  4. Enable at home commands all six legs to the home pose. The initial movement can jump. Send a pose or play the sequence only after checking alignment and clearance.

Pause holds the last commanded pose. Disable motors releases torque. When the training bridge is running, three seconds without communication also disables outputs. Keep the body supported. Full instructions ↓
